issues.problem: The English adds small factual details the Chinese does not have: Yimen is glossed as "the eastern gate of Daliang," Lord Xinling "called on him," the drive out happens "when everyone was seated," and he goes "with his carriage and escort." None contradict the Chinese, but they are additions to this field.
issues.suggestion: Trim the glosses to match the Chinese, e.g. drop "— the eastern gate of Daliang" and "and when everyone was seated," and render "亲自驾车去迎" simply as "drove out himself to fetch him."

issues.problem: Chinese says 公子矫魏王令代晋鄙 — he forged / falsely claimed the king's order — but the English only says he "announced that he came on the king's orders to replace Jin Bi," leaving out the fact that the order was forged at this point (it is stated later in story.8 and analysis.0).
issues.suggestion: Change to: "Lord Xinling announced, on a forged order from the king, that he was replacing Jin Bi."

issues.problem: The source is named 《史记·魏公子列传》 in Chinese, i.e. a liezhuan (biography) of the Lord of Wei (Xinling), but the English calls it the "Hereditary House of Lord Wei," the name used for a shijia section, and "Lord Wei" can be misread as the king of Wei.
issues.suggestion: Use "the 'Biography of Lord Wei' (Liezhuan) in the Records of the Grand Historian."

issues.problem: Same source-title mismatch as in limits.0: "Hereditary House of Lord Wei" for 《史记·魏公子列传》 (a liezhuan, not a hereditary house).
issues.suggestion: Use the same rendering as above, e.g. "one account in the 'Biography of Lord Wei' in the Records of the Grand Historian."

overall: The English edition matches the Chinese on all facts, dates, numbers, names, quotations and hedging markers; the only differences are a few harmless additions and renderings noted above.
